 Sunday, October 25, 2026 
 News 
 More residential premises spreading dengue mosquito 
 View(s): 
 By Nidarshani Wickramasinghe   
 The National Dengue Control Unit has decided to launch a seven-day dengue prevention programme in the first week of November.
 Community Physician Specialist Prashila Samaraweera said that an increase in larval density had been identified in high-risk Medical Officer of Health divisions in 13 districts. She pointed out that prompt action could help reduce the number of patients next month.
 Mosquito control programmes will be launched targeting 32 MOH divisions identified as dengue risk areas.
 Mosquito control programme in Maligakanda. Pic by Eshan Fernando
 Explaining the increase in mosquito larval density in many areas of the island at present, Dr Sakunthala Janaki, an entomologist at the National Dengue Control Unit, said a gradual increase has been observed in the percentage of mosquito breeding in houses.
 “According to the surveys we have done so far in October, if taken as a percentage, it is 8.7%. That means we are observing a gradual increase in the percentage of mosquito breeding in houses. Similarly, when government institutions are considered, the percentage that was around 17% in September has increased to around 33% in October.
 “We observed a decrease in reported dengue patients during August, September and October. Around August, we saw a reduction in our premises index to around 6.5%. However, by October, when considering the overall premises index across Sri Lanka, it is now being reported at around 9%. If the removal of mosquito breeding sites from premises is not carried out properly, we expect an increase in dengue patients within four to six weeks.”
 Commenting on this, Dr Kapila Kannangara, director of the National Dengue Control Unit, pointed out that due to the Northeast Monsoon rains and the El Nino conditions, water required for the life cycle of dengue mosquitoes could accumulate in the environment. There is a risk of dengue spreading with the rains.
 A total of 21,500 dengue patients were reported in June last year, while the number increased to 29,967 in July. However, he also said that the number of patients had fallen 10,155 in August and 5,130 in September.
 So far this year, more than 104,094 dengue patients have been reported, and 79 have died.
 Another death suspected to have been caused by dengue has also been reported but not confirmed. Investigations are being carried out, Dr Kannangara told the Sunday Times .
 Meanwhile, the highest number of reported dengue patients is in the Colombo District, while most of the remainder are in the districts of Gampaha, Kandy, Kalutara, Matara, Galle, Ratnapura, and Kegalle.
